newsitem.title: UK: Emerging market debt mixed on low volume.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt mixed on low volume.

text.p: Brady bond instruments were narrowly mixed on Tuesday but volume remained extremely light ahead of key U.S. economic data due to be released later this week, emerging market sources said.

"It is very quiet. There have been very few trades. Russia traded up slightly but that is the extent of any price movement today," said Chris Portman, assistant director of emerging markets research at ANZ Investment in London.
U.S. data to be released includes May U.S. retail sales on Thursday and May producer prices on Friday.
Market experts said the divergent views and uncertainty regarding the direction of U.S. interest rates kept many market participants on the sidelines.

"I think there is a bit of shyness on the buyside just on the expectancy that there is the potential for further (U.S. interest) rate rises," said a Brady bond trader at a major U.S. investment bank in London.
"The market feels more comfortable buying (emerging market debt) with (the 30-year U.S. Treasury) bonds at 6.95 percent rather than at 6.80," he added.
Currently, the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond is yielding 6.82 percent.
Still, improving fundamentals among emerging market countries should help to buoy prices, they said.
Russian Vneshekonombank dollar loans which have hovered near record highs for the past two days, were unchanged at 89-1/2 bid after rising 1/8 earlier today.
Market experts attributed the recent price gains on Russian loans mainly to growing optimism about the country's debt rescheduling with its commercial bank creditors.
Over the weekend, a Russian official said a date would be set in July for the signing of the rescheduling agreement.
Among other Eastern European debt instruments, Bulgarian FLRBs were 1/4 lower at 53 bid and the country's IABs were 1/4 higher at 68-7/8 bid. Poland's PDI bonds were unchanged at 85 bid.
More broadly, Latin American Brady bonds were mixed but some market participants said Venezuela and Ecuador still remained attractive at current levels.
"We are still very bullish on Venezuela," said Portman.

Though Venezuelan Brady bonds were largely unchanged on Tuesday, the country's $2.2 billion sale of its oil fields raised the spectre that some of the proceeds may be used to fund a Brady buyback, sources said.
Meanwhile, emerging market specialists said Ecuador could see further price gains after the government announces its specific economic measures.
"We could see a positive reaction if the (Ecuadorean) government shows signs of raising its taxation proposals, in particular, tax on local fuel prices," added Portman.
